| `esModuleInterop: false`, `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: false`, `alwaysStrict: false` | — | always-on; cannot be disabled |

TS 7 migration (PR #284, renovate/typescript-7.x, 2026-07-10): typescript@7.0.2 is the native Go compiler — the JS compiler API (`typescript/lib/typescript.js`) no longer ships. Next.js 16 stable can't load it (vercel/next.js#95490; fix is canary-only behind `experimental.useTypeScriptCli`).

**Shim in place:** `@typescript/native-preview` root devDep exists ONLY as a marker so `next build` takes its graceful native-compiler path and skips build-time type checking. Type safety is instead gated by the turbo `typecheck` task (native `tsc --noEmit`), which `build` depends on. **Remove the marker + consider reverting once Next stable supports typescript@7 natively.**

Non-obvious repo facts learned then:
- "CI" = the Vercel deploy of `apps/web` (has-toggle-dev-web) + Claude review actions. No GitHub Actions build/test; app/api local builds fail on missing Clerk env vars (pre-existing, unrelated to deps).
- `bun run check` (ultracite@latest) is broken locally/on main: "Could not resolve ultracite/core" — pre-existing, not in CI.
- tsup `dts` is disabled (needs the removed TS JS API); tsup is unmaintained, tsdown is the successor if the CLI ever needs .d.ts again.

content.text:
**CI is green on PR #284** — all checks pass (Vercel deployment of `web`, Claude review). The branch stays fully on `typescript@7.0.2`, with the commit `50325fb` pushed to `renovate/typescript-7.x`.

## What was actually broken

Not your code, and not your tsconfigs. TypeScript 7 is the native Go compiler: the npm package no longer ships the JS compiler API (`typescript/lib/typescript.js`) or `tsserver` — just a native `tsc` binary. Next.js 16.2.10's build-time type-check phase probes for exactly that missing file, concludes TypeScript "isn't installed," and fails the Vercel deploy. No stable Next.js supports TS 7 yet — the fix landed in canary literally today (2026-07-10, vercel/next.js#95490) behind `experimental.useTypeScriptCli`. Upgrading Next wouldn't have helped.

Meanwhile the repo itself is remarkably TS7-clean: I swept all 26 tsconfigs and the entire source for every option and construct removed in 7.0 (`baseUrl`, `outFile`, `moduleResolution: node`, ES5 target, namespaces, const enums, decorators, `export =`, JSDoc patterns) — zero hits. TS 6.0 was the deprecation bridge and this repo had already crossed it.

## The changes (6 files, +26/−4)

1. **`@typescript/native-preview` added as a root devDep** — purely a marker. Next 16 stable has a sanctioned code path: when it sees this package, it logs "Detected @typescript/native-preview as TypeScript compiler," writes `next-env.d.ts`, and skips its legacy type-check instead of erroring. Verified in Next's source and in the passing deploy.
2. **New turbo `typecheck` task, and `build` now depends on it** — this is the mitigation for the semantic change above. Skipping Next's check would have silently removed type checking from CI, so builds are now gated on the native `tsc --noEmit` instead (the existing per-workspace scripts, which were never wired into any pipeline). Bonus from the task graph: the `web` deploy also type-checks all 13 of its workspace dependencies. Verified it passes on a fresh-clone simulation (no `.next/`, no `next-env.d.ts`).
3. **`packages/email/templates/digest.tsx`** — annotated `DigestEmail`'s return type (`ReactElement`, matching the existing pattern in `welcome-to-waitlist.tsx`). This was the **one genuine TS7 semantic difference in the repo**: tsgo's stricter portability check (TS2883) rejects the inferred type; TS 6.0.3 accepted it.
4. **`packages/payments/index.ts`** — bumped the pinned Stripe `apiVersion` literal to `"2026-06-24.dahlia"`. **Pre-existing, not TS7**: it fails identically under 6.0.3 (from an earlier Stripe SDK bump) but had never surfaced because nothing ran `tsc` in CI. Note this pins your Stripe API behavior to the newer version the installed SDK is typed against — worth a glance if you rely on pre-June API behavior.
5. **`tsup.config.ts`** — `dts: false`. rollup-plugin-dts crashes under TS 7 (needs the removed JS API). Nothing is lost: the CLI's `files` array only ever published `dist/index.js`, so the `.d.ts` output was already dead weight. tsup is officially unmaintained; tsdown is the successor if you ever need declarations again.

## Semantic changes to be aware of (researched, not affecting this repo)

- 7.0 removes `ignoreDeprecations` — anything silenced with it under 6.x is a hard error. You used none.
- Template-literal type inference is now code-point based (emoji/surrogate pairs split differently); union ordering in errors/declarations is now deterministic (`stableTypeOrdering`, non-disableable); checked-JS/JSDoc support is heavily narrowed; parameters typed `any`/`unknown` can no longer be omitted at call sites. None of these patterns exist in your source.
- If any tool ever needs the old JS API back, the official escape hatch is aliasing: `"typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6"` + `"@typescript/native": "npm:typescript@7"` — that would restore byte-identical v6 behavior everywhere, at the cost of not really being on v7. I chose the marker approach instead since it keeps the real v7 compiler doing the checking.
- **Editors**: `tsserver` no longer exists; the language server is LSP-based (`tsc --lsp`). VS Code needs the "TypeScript Native Preview" extension until native support ships. The `"plugins": [{"name": "next"}]` tsconfig entry is a language-service plugin that the Go LSP may not load — editor-only, no build impact.

## Follow-ups

- **Remove the `@typescript/native-preview` marker** (and optionally revert to Next's built-in checking) once Next stable auto-detects typescript@7 — Vercel says that's coming before `useTypeScriptCli` stabilizes. I left a memory note.
- Two pre-existing issues I found but left alone: `bun run check` fails on `main` too ("Could not resolve ultracite/core"), and local `app`/`api` builds fail on missing Clerk env vars. Neither is in CI's path.
